---
title: "Baryon, dark-matter, and photon relative velocities"
---

## Velocities in the CMB frame

Use one physical frame for baryons, dark matter and photon dipoles. In physical
peculiar velocities, the homogeneous matter equations are

$$
\dot{\mathbf u}_b+H\mathbf u_b=\mathbf g+\mathbf f_b
 -\Gamma_b(\mathbf u_b-\mathbf u_\gamma),\qquad
\dot{\mathbf u}_c+H\mathbf u_c=\mathbf g.
$$

Consequently specifying only `u_b-u_c` does not determine the drag. A common
matter boost with the photon bath held fixed changes the physical problem.
The GPU source-aware path supports a zero fixed drag target; working in the
CMB coordinate frame is the supported choice. The evolved photon dipole may
still be nonzero in this frame.

The cosmological facade selects `scaling="jedamzik"`. Physical gas and photon
velocities are `V_ref*sqrt(a_ref/a)*v_code`, while particle velocities are
`1e4*L_h/a*v_particle`, with `L_h=cosmology.box_ckpc_h`. Never subtract their
unconverted stored arrays. Gas expansion multiplies its code velocity by
`sqrt(a_old/a_new)`; photon expansion multiplies its code velocity by
`sqrt(a_new/a_old)`, leaving the photon density monopole unchanged. The latter
keeps a homogeneous, unscattered physical photon dipole constant.

The corrected evolution is fingerprinted in checkpoints. A checkpoint from
before this correction cannot resume a corrected trajectory: restart from
consistent initial conditions. This prevents silently retaining an erroneous
pre-checkpoint photon history.

## Gravity source accuracy

Gravity remains a separate gas kick. A stiffly stable local drag solver does
not by itself make this splitting accurate. The default
`physics.gravity_drag_max_impulse=0.01` bounds the **outer** step's fast slip
impulse. It uses `Gamma_b*dt` with a fixed photon reservoir and
`(1+R_code)*Gamma_b*dt` with evolved photons. It is not replaced by particle
subcycling. The cap is finite and positive and is checkpointed.

For repeated final kicks against a frozen constant force, the steady slip
bias is `q/(1-exp(-q))-1`; at `q=0.01` this is about 0.501%. This is a useful
source-error scale, not a bound on all nonlinear errors. Decrease the cap to
demonstrate convergence of the target observable. The cap may reduce throughput
in strongly coupled, gravitating runs; it does not implement a joint implicit
gravity/MHD/photon integrator. Runs without gas gravity retain their source-aware
large-impulse updates.

## Comparing DM and gas velocity fields

`dm_v_x` is now the Fourier mode of a CIC mass/momentum velocity estimator on
the Eulerian gas mesh, evaluated at current particle positions. This replaces
the former transform over original lattice labels. Each cell averages the
velocities of deposited particles with the same weights as its deposited mass.
The mode is converted with the physical cosmology box, independently of
`MHD_BOXSIZE`. The mode wavenumber likewise uses the physical box.

The diagnostic reuses two integrator scratch grids after the force modes have
been reduced and before the next evolution step. The deposition and mode
reduction complete before those buffers are reused for another component.
No additional full-grid velocity/density allocations are retained per output.
Photon maps likewise inverse-transform a copy in the reusable radiation
workspace, since a multidimensional real inverse FFT may overwrite its input.
Output requests must not modify the persistent photon modes. The production
validator compares sparse and frequent diagnostics through coupled evolution.

Empty cells are assigned zero in this estimator; the output also reports
`dm_velocity_empty_fraction`. An appreciable empty fraction requires a different
estimator or a resolved mesh before interpreting a volume-weighted gas/DM
comparison. After shell crossing, the DM mean velocity also does not describe
the full velocity distribution. `dm_displacement_x` remains a lattice-label
displacement diagnostic and must not be treated as an Eulerian velocity.

## Validation

`test/test_relative_velocities.jl` checks expansion units, the fast-slip source
cap, the phase of translated Eulerian particle velocities, physical box units,
and rejection of checkpoints made before the photon correction. Shared backend
checks also exercise repeated deposition, empty cells, and photon rescaling on
the explicitly requested real device.

`tools.reference.homogeneous_velocities` independently integrates physical
baryon, photon, and CDM velocities with fixed ionization using SciPy Radau.
`scripts/validate_relative_velocities.jl` compares the actual production driver
against this oracle and checks timestep refinement. A separate displaced-DM
lattice case starts all velocities at zero, generates a nonzero periodic
Poisson force, and refines the gravity/drag cap at a common endpoint. It checks
signed complex baryon–photon slip against a finer temporal reference on the same
grid, with signal floors and tolerances declared before execution. This does
not supply an independent nonlinear gravity oracle or spatial convergence.

Run from the repository root with a new output directory:

```sh
julia --project=. -t 4 scripts/validate_relative_velocities.jl results/velocity-cpu-f32 f32
julia --project=. -t 4 scripts/validate_relative_velocities.jl results/velocity-cpu-f64 f64
```

The validator clears unrelated `MHD_*` shell settings and records source/oracle
hashes, resolved settings, raw complex-mode comparisons, actual endpoints and
checkpoints. Chemistry is disabled and ionization is fixed to isolate velocity
transport; these are controlled limits, not a converged recombination calculation.
